subject: def-rpm-h-background-and-model-quantities

actual_judge.reason: The unit convention contradicts itself: with x^a in metres and p_a in momentum units, p=p_a dx^a has action units. The item assigns momentum units to this covector, then action units to the same expression. Momentum units belong to the components p_a.

smallest_missing_premise: None: the existing exact cotangent supplier already assigns component units action divided by coordinate units. The local sentence incorrectly attaches the momentum unit to the full covector expression rather than the fibre components.
repair: Change only the grammatical subject from cotangent vector p=p_a dx^a to its fibre components p_a. Keep all formulas, canonical one-form/action units, proper-time/observer conventions, physical scope and dependencies exact.
supplier_support: For an interpreted particle model, assign coordinates $q^i$ their declared units and assign the conjugate covector components $p_i$ units of action divided by the units of $q^i$. Thus $\theta$ and $\omega$ have action units, conventionally joule-seconds

current_public_and_fact_excerpts_read.text:
On $\mathbb R^4$, set $N=1$, $h_{ij}=\delta_{ij}$, and $\beta=(2,0,0)$. The metric is

$$g=-(dx^0)^2+(dx^1+2dx^0)^2+(dx^2)^2+(dx^3)^2.$$

It is flat under $X^0=x^0, X^1=x^1+2x^0, X^2=x^2, X^3=x^3$, with time orientation $T=\partial/\partial X^0=\partial_0-2\partial_1$. Explicitly, a nonzero causal vector $v$ is future-directed when $g(v,T)<0$, so increasing $X^0$ is future. The chart remains temporal with future unit normal $n=T$. For a massive state $m>0$ with spatial momentum $p=(p_1,0,0)$, $p_1>mc/\sqrt3$, the future shell has

$$H=c\left(\sqrt{m^2c^2+p_1^2}-2p_1\right)<0,$$

but the normal-observer energy $E_n=c\sqrt{m^2c^2+p_1^2}>0$. The coordinate speed magnitude exceeds $c$, while the local normal-observer speed remains below $c$.

**Given:** The flat metric, time orientation and chart coefficients above, $m>0$, $c>0$, and a spatial momentum satisfying $p_1>mc/\sqrt3$.

[A1] [[def-countable-choice]]: Assume countable choice ACω, meaning every sequence of nonempty sets has a choice function; no full Axiom of Choice is assumed.

[F1] [[def-rpm-h-temporal-chart-data]]: lapse-shift data define a temporal chart and normal field.

[F2] [[thm-rpm-h-temporal-shell-reduction]]: future-root chart Hamiltonian is $H=c(N\kappa-\beta^ip_i)$.

[F3] [[def-rpm-h-background-and-model-quantities]]: normal-observer energy is $E_n=-c\,p(n)$, defined from the supplied future unit observer.

current_affected_use_checks.reason: Its p1, kappa and p(n) are component/evaluation variables already in momentum units, H/E are c times those variables in joules. Compatible with supplier correction. A separate new velocity-definition objection is queued and is not discharged by this unit review.

current_public_and_fact_excerpts_read.text:
Let $I\subset\mathbb R$ be an open interval, and let $x:I\to M$ be a $C^2$ future-directed timelike worldline on a prescribed smooth, time-oriented Lorentzian background $(M,g,T)$ of signature $(-+++)$, with $m>0$ a fixed primitive mass in kg and $c>0$ in m/s. For any compact segment $[a,b]\subset I$ with $a<b$, adopt the stationary-action model on that segment

$$S_{m,[a,b]}[x]=-mc\int_a^b\sqrt{-g(x',x') }\,d\lambda.$$

Here $I\subset\mathbb R$ is an open interval, $\lambda$ is its real coordinate, and $x'$ denotes $dx/d\lambda$. The future-timelike condition makes $x'$ nowhere zero. On a neighborhood of $[a,b]$, $x$ is $C^2$ (so its tangent is $C^1$). If $\widetilde\lambda=f(\lambda)$ is an increasing $C^1$ reparametrization with $f'>0$, then $\sqrt{-g(dx/d\widetilde\lambda,dx/d\widetilde\lambda)}\,d\widetilde\lambda=\sqrt{-g(x',x')}\,d\lambda$ by the chain rule. An admissible variation is a family $x_\epsilon(\lambda)$ defined for $\epsilon\in(-\delta,\delta)$, $\delta>0$, and $\lambda$ in a common neighborhood of $[a,b]$, with $x_0=x$, that is $C^2$ jointly in $(\epsilon,\lambda)$, has fixed endpoint events $x_\epsilon(a)=x(a)$ and $x_\epsilon(b)=x(b)$, and remains future timelike for sufficiently small $|\epsilon|$. The adopted motion principle is that on every such segment $[a,b]$, the physical worldline $x$ satisfies $\left.\frac{d}{d\epsilon}\right|_{\epsilon=0}S_{m,[a,b]}[x_\epsilon]=0$ for every admissible variation through $x$. The integrand is the proper-time length density, so $S_{m,[a,b]}=-mc^2\int_a^b d\tau$; its dimension is action (J s). The adopted premise concerns this ideal free test body only. It is neither a theorem about all matter nor an empirical report, and supplies no backreaction or completeness claim. The flat ideal-clock specialization agrees with [[post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light]]; adopting this action on a curved background remains a separate premise.

The cotangent phase-space carrier convention assumes countable choice ACω only; full choice is not assumed.

current_affected_use_checks.reason: Length action -mc integral s d_lambda is action; no assumption that the coordinate covector expression has momentum units. Separate source-description objection queued, unchanged science used here.

current_public_and_fact_excerpts_read.text:
On a prescribed background $(M,g,T)$, choose an open parameter interval $I$ and a compact segment $[a,b]\subset I$ with $a<b$. In a spacetime chart containing the curve and sufficiently small variations, let $x:I\to M$ be smooth near $[a,b]$, let $p(\lambda)\in T^*_{x(\lambda)}M$ be a smooth covector field along $x$, and let $e$ be smooth and positive near $[a,b]$. In this chart, write $g_{ab}=g(\partial_a,\partial_b)$ for $a,b\in\{0,1,2,3\}$, let $(g^{ab})$ be the inverse matrix, and define $p^\sharp=\sum_{a,b=0}^3g^{ab}p_b\partial_a$; equivalently, $g(p^\sharp,w)=p(w)$ for every tangent vector $w$. Adopt the distinct massless classical particle action on this segment

$$S_{0,[a,b]}[x,p,e]=\int_a^b\left[p_a x'^a-eC_0(x,p)\right]d\lambda,\qquad C_0=\tfrac12g^{ab}p_ap_b.$$

Admissible variations are smooth one-parameter families of chart fields $(x_\epsilon,p_\epsilon,e_\epsilon)$ on a common neighborhood of $[a,b]$, with $x_\epsilon(a)=x(a)$ and $x_\epsilon(b)=x(b)$; the $p_\epsilon$ and $e_\epsilon$ variations are independent and have no endpoint constraints, while $e_\epsilon>0$ for sufficiently small $|\epsilon|$. Impose the physical branch only on stationary solutions after these variations: $p\ne0$ and $p^\sharp$ is future null. With all spacetime coordinates measured in metres and dimensionless $\lambda$, $p_a$ has units kg m/s, $C_0$ has units kg²m²/s² and $e$ has units s/kg, making the action J s. Other parameter units scale $e$ accordingly. This is a separate adopted model: null curves have no proper-time parameter, the model does not arise by setting $m=0$ in $P=mU$, and its positive momentum scale is additional initial data. On the nonzero branch, the vertical differential is $d_pC_0=p^\sharp\ne0$: nondegeneracy of $g^{-1}$ and $p\ne0$ give $p^\sharp\ne0$. Hence the shell is a regular primary constraint in the sense of [[def-rpm-h-regular-constraint-system]]. This postulate is not an empirical observation or a deduction from the massive model.

The cotangent phase-space carrier convention assumes countable choice ACω only; full choice is not assumed.

current_affected_use_checks.reason: Explicitly assigns momentum units to p_a and integrates p_a x-prime-a d_lambda; this is exactly the corrected component/action convention.

current_public_and_fact_excerpts_read.text: Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an interval with nonempty interior, and let $\gamma:I\to M$ be a $C^1$ future-timelike curve on a prescribed smooth Lorentzian background, parameterized by $\lambda$; set $V=d\gamma/d\lambda$. For the massive square-root Lagrangian $L=-mc\sqrt{-g(V,V)}$ with $m,c>0$, its fibre derivative is $p=mc\,V^\flat/\sqrt{-g(V,V)}$. If $\tau$ is proper time along $\gamma$, then $U=d\gamma/d\tau=cV/\sqrt{-g(V,V)}$, so the raised momentum is $p^\sharp=mU$. In flat spacetime this agrees with the adopted special-relativistic mechanical momentum convention. This is a model identity, not a measurement.

**Given:** A future timelike $C^1$ worldline on a smooth Lorentzian background, $m>0$, $c>0$, and the square-root action model.

[A1] [[def-countable-choice]]: Assume countable choice ACω, meaning every sequence of nonempty sets has a choice function; no full Axiom of Choice is assumed.

[F1] [[def-gr-timelike-worldline-and-proper-time]] supplies $d\tau=\sqrt{-g(V,V)}d\lambda/c$ on a future-timelike curve, and $U=dx/d\tau$. The parameter and SI quantity conventions are those of [[def-rpm-h-background-and-model-quantities]].

[F2] [[thm-rpm-h-homogeneous-massive-shell]]: fibre derivative of $L=-mc\sqrt{-g(V,V)}$ is $p=mcV^\flat/s$.

[F3] [[post-sr-massive-particle-dynamics]] adopts the flat massive-particle mechanical momentum $P=mU$, with its component identities supplied by [[pthm-sr-momentum-and-four-force]]. The geometric four-velocity and proper-time relation are supplied by [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]].

[F4] [[post-rpm-h-free-test-particle-action]]: the massive square-root action is the adopted free-particle model.

[F5] [[thm-rpm-h-first-order-action-and-geodesics]]: for a smooth stationary first-order triple on the future massive branch with positive multiplier, its canonical covector equals the square-root fibre derivative. This comparison requires that supplier's stationary-triple hypotheses.

current_affected_use_checks.reason: Fibre derivative and raised identity p-sharp=mU are unchanged. F1 proper-time and SI conventions concern derivative components; no whole one-form momentum-unit claim is required.

current_public_and_fact_excerpts_read.text:
Under the hypotheses of [[thm-rpm-h-temporal-shell-reduction]], all lapse, shift and spatial-metric coefficients in the reduced expressions below are evaluated at the spacetime event $(ct,q)$, as in the temporal-shell supplier; $n$ is the normal at that same event. The future unit normal $n=N^{-1}(\partial_0-\beta^i\partial_i)$ measures positive particle energy

$$E_n=-c\,p(n)=c\kappa,$$

while the chart's reduced Hamiltonian is $H=c(N\kappa-\beta^ip_i)$. The normal-frame spatial velocity is $w^i=(\dot q^i/c+\beta^i)/N=h^{ij}p_j/\kappa$, with $h_{ij}w^iw^j<1$ for $m>0$ and $=1$ for a nonzero massless state. Write $|\beta|_h:=\sqrt{h_{ij}\beta^i\beta^j}$ and $|p|_{h^{-1}}:=\sqrt{h^{ij}p_ip_j}$. If $\beta^2:=h_{ij}\beta^i\beta^j<N^2$, then $H>0$. If $\beta^2>N^2$, $H$ can be negative even though $E_n>0$. Along a Hamiltonian solution, $dH/dt=\partial_tH$; explicit time independence is sufficient for its conservation. On a connected solution interval, $H(t,q(t),p(t))$ is constant if and only if $\partial_tH(t,q(t),p(t))=0$ throughout that interval.

**Given:** A lapse-shift temporal chart, positive $N,h$, a future shell state, and a solution of its reduced equations.

[A1] [[def-countable-choice]]: Assume countable choice ACω, meaning every sequence of nonempty sets has a choice function; no full Axiom of Choice is assumed.

[F1] [[def-rpm-h-background-and-model-quantities]]: $p$ is a covector and an observer is a future unit timelike vector.

[F2] [[def-rpm-h-temporal-chart-data]]: $n=N^{-1}(\partial_0-\beta^i\partial_i)$, $g(n,n)=-1$, and $h$ is positive definite.

[F3] [[thm-rpm-h-temporal-shell-reduction]]: κ, shell root and $H=c(N\kappa-\beta^ip_i)$ as displayed.

[F4] [[pthm-sr-momentum-and-four-force]]: in the flat specialization, energy is the time component paired with the inertial observer; this supplier is not assumed on curved backgrounds.

[F5] [[post-rpm-h-free-test-particle-action]]: the massive branch is an adopted square-root test-particle model.

[F6] [[post-rpm-h-massless-shell-action]]: the massless branch is a separate model with nonzero future-null momentum.

current_affected_use_checks.reason: Uses covector evaluation on a future unit normal and coordinate components p0,pi; kappa/coordinate momentum carry momentum units and c kappa is energy. F1 says p is a covector, not that p_a dx^a itself has momentum units.

current_public_and_fact_excerpts_read.text: Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ for the moment-map supplier. Adopt either the massive free test-particle action or the distinct massless shell action of [[post-rpm-h-free-test-particle-action]] and [[post-rpm-h-massless-shell-action]]. Conditional on those model choices and the corresponding future free-shell equations, the affine Poincaré charges are conserved on flat spacetime; in a fixed-time Hamiltonian description the boost charge includes its explicit partial-time derivative. On a prescribed curved background, every mechanical scalar $p_a\xi^a$ for a Killing field is conserved along the adopted free shell. These are model deductions. They do not establish the empirical adequacy of either action, and they do not extend to arbitrary interacting potentials.

**Given:** A flat inertial Minkowski background or a prescribed smooth Lorentzian background with a Killing field, and one of the explicitly adopted free-particle models.

[A1] [[post-rpm-h-free-test-particle-action]]: the massive model adopts fixed primitive mass $m>0$ and the stationary action $-mc\int\sqrt{-g(x',x')}d\lambda$ on future timelike curves with the stated endpoint and regularity conditions. The H5 carrier remains a draft adopted postulate with no pipeline_run binding; its current Step 1 record is ready/hash-current, which is input readiness and not empirical evidence or independent proof approval.

[A2] [[post-rpm-h-massless-shell-action]]: the massless model is a separate constrained first-order action with nonzero future null momentum and positive multiplier; it is not obtained by putting $m=0$ in the massive square-root action. This H5 carrier remains a draft adopted postulate with no pipeline_run binding; its current Step 1 record is ready/hash-current, not an empirical finding or independent proof approval.

[L1] [[thm-rpm-h-poincare-moment-map-and-algebra]]: the current assigned A draft states shell charge descent and the time-dependent boost identity partial_t B_i+{B_i,E}=0. It is a batch-26 draft with H0/H8 inputs still open.

[L2] [[thm-rpm-h-killing-shell-first-integral]]: for a Killing vector, $\{p_a\xi^a,C_m\}=0$ identically, so the scalar is conserved along the constrained free-shell flow; the proof is conditional on H0/H7.

[A3] [[def-countable-choice]]: assume countable choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ only; no full axiom of choice is used.

[L3] [[thm-rpm-h-first-order-action-and-geodesics]]: the current H7 draft assumes a prescribed smooth time-oriented Lorentzian background, a compact chart interval, smooth $x,p,e$, $e>0$, and either the future timelike $m>0$ branch or the separate nonzero future-null $m=0$ branch; its stationary equations are $x\prime{}^a=e g^{ab}p_b$, $p\prime{}_a=-\tfrac e2\partial_a g^{bc}p_bp_c$, $C_m=0$. It relates the massive square-root functional to the shell equations; the null branch remains separately specified. This is a mathematical variational supplier for explicit functionals and selected future branches; adoption of particle dynamics is a separate physical premise.

current_affected_use_checks.reason: No new unit assertion; canonical charge contractions and action-model consequences retain same formulas and their declared geometric generators.

current_public_and_fact_excerpts_read.text:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ for the cotangent/H7/H9 supplier chain. Adopt the massive free action or separate massless shell action in [[post-rpm-h-free-test-particle-action]] and [[post-rpm-h-massless-shell-action]]. Let $I_0\subseteq\mathbb R$ be the open first-coordinate interval, measured in metres, of a temporal product chart, and let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be its open spatial coordinate range. Let $(N,\beta,h)$ be the smooth temporal-chart data on $I_0\times\Omega$ of [[def-rpm-h-temporal-chart-data]], with $N>0$ and $h_{ij}$ positive definite. Take $m\ge0$ in kg and $c>0$ in m/s, and define the physical-time domain $I_t:=\{t\in\mathbb R:ct\in I_0\}$ and pulled-back data $\widehat N(t,q):=N(ct,q)$, $\widehat\beta^i(t,q):=\beta^i(ct,q)$, $\widehat h_{ij}(t,q):=h_{ij}(ct,q)$. Write $\widehat h^{ij}$ for the inverse matrix. On the future shell with $x^0=ct$, define $\kappa(t,q,p)=\sqrt{m^2c^2+\widehat h^{ij}(t,q)p_ip_j}$, $p_0=\widehat\beta^i p_i-\widehat N\kappa$, and the positive-root reduced Hamiltonian $H(t,q,p)=-cp_0=c\bigl(\widehat N\kappa-\widehat\beta^ip_i\bigr)$ from [[thm-rpm-h-temporal-shell-reduction]]. Its open domain is $U=I_t\times T^*\Omega$ for $m>0$, and $U=I_t\times(T^*\Omega\setminus\{p=0\})$ for $m=0$. Here $t$ is measured in seconds, $q$ in metres, $p$ in kg m/s, $H$ in joules, and $S$ in joule-seconds. Let $D\subseteq I_t\times\Omega$ be open and let $S\in C^2(D,\mathbb R)$ (all partial derivatives through order two are continuous) satisfy $S_t+H(t,q,S_q)=0$ wherever $(t,q,S_q)\in U$. If $S$ is the smooth local solution supplied by [[thm-rpm-h-local-hamilton-jacobi]] from an initial exact-graph point in $U$, and $J=[t_1,t_2]\subset I_t$ with $t_1<t_2$ is an interval on which its characteristic projection remains invertible, let $q:J\to\Omega$ be a $C^1$ characteristic with $\dot q=H_p(t,q,S_q)$. Then $p(t):=S_q(t,q(t))$ satisfies $\dot p=-H_q$, so $(q,p)$ obey Hamilton's equations. The smooth ODE makes this characteristic smooth; by [[thm-rpm-h-temporal-shell-reduction]] these reduced equations are exactly the equations of the future-shell first-order system of [[thm-rpm-h-first-order-action-and-geodesics]]. Under the matching adopted model postulate, this curve is a trajectory of the massive or separate massless model. The conclusion holds only on the chart and the actual invertible projection interval; no global Hamilton--Jacobi graph continuation is asserted. It is a conditional mathematical prediction, not a reported observation.

The characteristic graph is restricted to points with $(t,q,S_q(t,q))\in U$. The action $S$ is measured in joule-seconds.

**Given:** One of the stated free-particle model postulates, the temporal chart and future-shell domain, a smooth HJ solution, and a characteristic curve on a compact interval of its invertible projection.

[A3] [[def-countable-choice]]: assume countable choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ only for the cotangent/H7 supplier chain; no full axiom of choice is used.

[A1] [[post-rpm-h-free-test-particle-action]]: the massive action is adopted only for future timelike curves and fixed $m>0$ with the stated regularity and endpoint conditions. This H5 carrier remains a draft model postulate with no pipeline_run binding; its current Step 1 record is ready/hash-current, which does not make it an empirical report or independent proof approval.

[A2] [[post-rpm-h-massless-shell-action]]: the massless model separately adopts nonzero future null momentum and a positive multiplier; it has no massive proper-time parameterization. This H5 carrier remains a draft model postulate with no pipeline_run binding; its current Step 1 record is ready/hash-current and is not an empirical report or independent proof approval.

[L1] [[thm-rpm-h-first-order-action-and-geodesics]]: the current H7 draft assumes a prescribed smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold, a compact chart interval, smooth $x,p,e$, $e>0$, $m\ge0$, and the future massive or separate nonzero future-null branch. It supplies $C_m=0$, $x\prime{}^a=e g^{ab}p_b$, $p\prime{}_a=-\tfrac e2\partial_a g^{bc}p_bp_c$, and the unparameterized geodesic interpretation. This is a mathematical variational supplier for explicit functionals and selected future branches; adoption of particle dynamics is a separate physical premise.

[L2] [[thm-rpm-h-local-hamilton-jacobi]]: when the initial exact-graph point lies in its open Hamiltonian domain, it supplies a smooth local HJ solution while the characteristic projection remains invertible. Its proof uses the current draft canonical-flow supplier's stated local Hamiltonian equations; that supplier's Step 1 readiness is not independent proof approval.

[L3] [[thm-rpm-h-complete-integral-coordinates]]: for a nonsingular mixed Hessian, the HJ parameters and their conjugates give local canonical integration coordinates; the item states the exact chart and projection-invertibility limitation.

[L4] [[thm-rpm-h-temporal-shell-reduction]]: at the point $x^0=ct$ in the chart, under $N>0$, positive-definite $h$, and nonzero spatial momentum on the massless branch, the positive future-shell root gives $p_0=\beta^i(ct,q)p_i-N(ct,q)\kappa$, $H=-cp_0$, and $C_{p_0}=\kappa/N>0$ for $C=\tfrac12(g^{ab}p_ap_b+m^2c^2)$. Its gauge-reduced action has Hamilton equations on the chart interval. This current H9 supplier is a draft; the use here is conditional on that exact statement.

current_affected_use_checks.reason: Explicit t seconds, q metres, p component coordinates kg m/s and S joule-seconds; p=S_q is the exact corrected convention.

current_public_and_fact_excerpts_read.text: In the flat inertial-time model of [[thm-rpm-h-inertial-time-reduced-hamiltonian]], the coordinate velocity is $\dot{\mathbf q}=c^2\mathbf p/E$. For $m>0$, its Euclidean magnitude is strictly less than $c$; for the separate massless model $m=0$ with $\mathbf p\ne0$, its magnitude is exactly $c$. Spatial momentum is constant in both cases. These are deductions from the adopted free actions, not experimental measurements.

**Given:** Flat inertial coordinates, $c>0$, either the massive model with $m>0$ or the separately postulated nonzero-null model.

[A1] [[def-countable-choice]]: Assume countable choice ACω, meaning every sequence of nonempty sets has a choice function; no full Axiom of Choice is assumed.

[F1] [[post-rpm-h-free-test-particle-action]]: the massive square-root action is the adopted free model.

[F2] [[post-rpm-h-massless-shell-action]]: the massless branch is separately postulated with nonzero spatial momentum.

[F3] [[thm-rpm-h-inertial-time-reduced-hamiltonian]]: $E=\sqrt{m^2c^4+c^2|\mathbf p|^2}$, $\dot q=c^2\mathbf p/E$, and $\dot p=0$.

current_affected_use_checks.reason: Energy/momentum/velocity identities already use spatial components p; corrected component units preserve c-squared p/E as metres per second.
